items.note: The page asserts 'A fixed output coefficient averages rM signed scalar products' with a citation and then concludes the contraction. It does not give the matching argument that produces the count rM.

Every part of the procedure is on the page: 'Perform both forward transforms and retain their common LB order', products by Signed packing truncated by Q_p, 'passing the product to the opposite transform without reordering', and the final scaling by M.

The page writes F^- explicitly with the 1/M normalization and uses chi_j(k+l)=chi_j(k)chi_j(l), which holds because omega_{t_i}^{t_i}=1, together with commutativity. Expanding the double sum gives (1/M)(M F^-f)(M F^-g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g), and the algebra is correct.
F^+F^-=I/M is obtained by tensoring the per-axis identity F_t^+F_t^-=I/t. Applying F^+ gives (f*g)/M=MF^+((F^-f)(F^-g)), and dividing by r gives the identity, as in the paper.

'Since P acts on each record separately, P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v). Because T_+LB=F^+ ...' is the paper's argument, made slightly more explicit. Both permutations are said to 'move whole records and leave each record's polynomial intact'.
delta=sqrt2 l 2^{-p} is introduced as the error of each transform procedure, citing the lemma, and eta=sqrt2 2^{-p} as the error of one truncation Q_p. Both values match the paper.

The page proves the bilinear bound on P from the r signed products per coefficient. It splits P(u~,v~)-P(u,v)=P(u~-u,v~)+P(u,v~-v) and bounds each term by delta using norm at most 1 of v~ and u, as the paper does.
'truncation gives ||z~-z_*||<2delta+eta' follows from the triangle inequality and the truncation bound. The page records that Q_p keeps the product in the disk, but in the Cost section, not here.

The page uses the opposite procedure's error delta on z~, and the contraction property of T_+, which it justifies ('F^+ averages signed shifts and B^{-1}L^{-1} only permutes records'). The triangle inequality then gives <3delta+eta, matching the paper's display.
The page uses MT_+z_*=M_r(f,g), shown earlier, so exact scaling by M gives M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}. The arithmetic is correct.
